children: was held liable by a German court for fraudulent advertisements posted by third parties on Facebook and Instagram, with the company ordered to remove the content and pay damages.

The case was brought by the operator of a German financial portal and its founder after their trademarked logo and image were used without permission in posts promoting allegedly fraudulent investments. The portal operator reported almost 260 violations to Meta
in August 2024 alone, with some content taking as long as 62 days to be removed, according to the court.

could not invoke the Digital Services Act’s lack-of-knowledge defense, saying the company exercises control over content through its algorithms and advertising practices. The court cited a June ruling by the European Court of Justice as precedent.
said it disagrees with the decision and is considering its next steps, while pointing to measures including proactive detection and removal of reported content.
must also disclose information about the fake advertisements and revenue generated from them. The decision is not final and can be challenged through an appeal, the court said.

title: Meta faces German court ruling over fake ads on Facebook, Instagram
